title: Ros Omelette
steps: Beat eggs with salt. Make a fluffy omelette on a hot pan.
Heat the ros (gravy) separately. Place the omelette on a plate and pour the hot gravy generously over it.
Top with chopped onion, green chilli and coriander. Serve immediately with soft Goan pao or poi.

fullIngredients.name: Leftover chicken or mutton xacuti / ros gravy

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Street-food classic – best with leftover spicy xacuti-style gravy.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The contrast of soft omelette and rich, spicy ros is the signature.

title: Pão Bhaji (Goan Style)
steps: Prepare a mildly spiced vegetable or dried-pea bhaji tempered with coconut and local spices.
Warm the fresh Goan bread (pao/poi).
Serve the hot bhaji with the bread for dunking.

fullIngredients.name: Mixed vegetables or dried peas / potato bhaji

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday Goan breakfast – fresh bakery bread is essential.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Hindu and Catholic homes both enjoy variations of this.

title: Sanna
steps: Soak rice, grind with coconut into a smooth batter. Ferment with toddy or yeast overnight until light and airy.
Add a little sugar and salt. Pour into greased moulds or idli plates.
Steam for 12–15 minutes till soft and spongy.
Serve with sorpotel, vindaloo or any spicy curry, or simply with coconut.

fullIngredients.name: Sugar, yeast or traditional toddy starter

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Goan equivalent of idli, traditionally fermented with toddy (palm sap).

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Soft, slightly sweet and perfect for mopping up rich gravies.

title: Fish Curry Rice (Xit Kodi)
steps: Grind coconut with red chillies, coriander, garlic and a little water into a smooth paste.
Extract kokum or tamarind water. Sauté onion and curry leaves, add the masala paste and kokum water. Bring to a boil.
Gently add fish pieces and simmer on low heat till cooked. Do not over-stir.
Serve with steamed rice, fried fish, sol kadhi and pickle.

fullIngredients.name: Kokum or tamarind, red chillies, turmeric, coriander, garlic

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The everyday staple of Goan homes – Xit (rice) + Kodi (curry).

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Fresh fish and coconut are non-negotiable for authentic flavour.

title: Pork Vindaloo
steps: Grind chillies, garlic, spices with vinegar into a paste. Marinate pork for several hours or overnight.
Heat oil, brown onions, add the marinated pork and cook on medium heat. Add a little water if needed and simmer till the meat is tender and the gravy is thick and tangy.
The dish should be spicy, sour and deeply aromatic.
Serve with sannas, pao or rice.

fullIngredients.name: Goan vinegar or palm vinegar, garlic, dried red chillies
Cumin, mustard seeds, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Derived from Portuguese 'vinha d'alhos' (wine & garlic); traditional Goan version uses palm vinegar and no potatoes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best made a day ahead – flavours improve.

title: Chicken Xacuti
steps: Dry-roast coconut and whole spices; grind into a fine paste with a little water.
Sauté onion, ginger-garlic and tomato. Add the xacuti masala and cook till oil separates.
Add chicken, salt and tamarind extract. Simmer till chicken is cooked and gravy is thick and aromatic.
Serve with rice, pao or poi.

fullIngredients.name: Poppy seeds, dried red chillies, peppercorns, fennel, cinnamon, star anise

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: One of Goa's most complex and fragrant curries – the roasted coconut and whole spices define it.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Leftover gravy is excellent for Ros Omelette.

title: Chicken Cafreal
steps: Grind coriander, green chillies, garlic, ginger and whole spices with lime/vinegar into a bright green paste.
Marinate chicken thoroughly for at least 1–2 hours.
Cook in a pan with a little oil on medium heat till the chicken is done and the masala coats it well (can also be grilled).
Serve with salad, fries or pao.

fullIngredients.name: Fresh coriander leaves, green chillies, garlic, ginger
Cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, lime juice or vinegar

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Believed to have African (Mozambican) roots via Portuguese influence.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The vibrant green colour and fresh coriander flavour are signature.

title: Sorpotel
steps: Boil the pork pieces and offal separately, cool and dice into small cubes.
Grind chillies, garlic, ginger and spices with vinegar into a paste.
Fry the diced meat, add the masala and onions, and cook slowly with vinegar and a little stock till the gravy is thick, dark and intensely spicy-sour.
Best made 1–2 days ahead. Serve with sannas or pao.

fullIngredients.name: Goan vinegar, dried red chillies, garlic, ginger

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Festive and wedding centrepiece of Goan Catholic cuisine.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The vinegar and slow cooking develop deep, complex flavour.

title: Choriz Pão
steps: Remove chouriço from casings or slice. Fry in a pan till the fat renders and the sausage is cooked and slightly crisp. Add sliced onion and a splash of vinegar if desired.
Split the warm pao, stuff generously with the cooked choriz mixture.
Serve hot as a snack or light meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Goan street and home snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The spicy, vinegary sausage is the star – good bread is essential.

title: Prawn Rissois
steps: Make a thick béchamel, mix in sautéed prawns, onion, chilli and coriander. Cool completely.
Shape into small crescents or ovals, dip in egg and coat with breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry till golden and crisp.
Serve hot as a tea-time or party snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Portuguese-influenced Goan tea-time favourite.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Creamy prawn filling and crisp coating are key.

title: Khatkhate
steps: Cook dal and vegetables separately or together till soft.
Grind coconut with chillies and spices. Add to the vegetables along with tamarind extract and simmer.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in oil and pour over.
Serve with rice as a mixed-vegetable stew.

fullIngredients.name: Mixed vegetables (pumpkin, brinjal, beans, potato, drumstick, etc.)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional Goan Hindu mixed-vegetable dish, often festive.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Showcases seasonal local produce.

title: Sol Kadhi
steps: Soak kokum in warm water, extract the pinkish liquid.
Mix with fresh coconut milk, crushed green chilli, garlic, cumin and salt.
Chill if desired. Garnish with coriander.
Serve as a cooling digestive drink with fish curry rice or any Goan meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Essential accompaniment and digestive in Goan thalis.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The kokum gives a unique sour-pink colour and flavour.

title: Bebinca
steps: Mix coconut milk, egg yolks, sugar, flour and nutmeg into a smooth batter.
In a baking dish, pour a thin layer of batter and bake or grill till set and golden. Brush with ghee.
Repeat layering and baking until all batter is used (traditionally 7–16 layers).
Cool completely, slice and serve.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic multi-layered Goan dessert, traditionally baked in a clay oven.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Time-consuming but the caramelised layers are worth it.
